question.text: Consider a thin square plate floating on a viscous liquid in a large tank. The height <math><mi>h</mi></math> of the liquid in the tank is much less than the width of the tank. The floating plate is pulled horizontally with a constant velocity <math><msub><mrow><mi>u</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub></math> . Which of the following statements is (are) true?

options.text: The resistive force of liquid on the plate is inversely proportional to  <math><mi>h</mi></math>
The resistive force of liquid on the plate is independent of the area of the plate
The tangential (shear) stress on the floor of the tank increases with <math><msub><mrow><mi>u</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub></math>
The tangential (shear) stress on the plate varies linearly with the viscosity <math><mi>η</mi></math> of the liquid

solution.text:
Viscous force is given by F=-ηAdvdy since h is very small therefore, magnitude of viscous force is given by
F=-ηA∆v∆y
∴  F=ηAu0h⇒F∝η and F∝u0;F∝1h,F∝A
Since plate is moving with constant velocity, same force must be acting on the floor
